flawed_step: 0022: Because paths were defined to have positive length, reachability in a DAG is irreflexive, not a reflexive partial order; it would need to be called a strict partial order.
counterexample: Let V={a,b} and E={(a,b),(b,a)}. This G is cyclic, and GT contains all four ordered pairs. Any graph with closure GT must provide reachability in both directions, requiring at least two edges; the only two-edge graph that does so is {(a,b),(b,a)}. Thus G has a unique transitive reduction despite being cyclic.
